parts.released_note: service

specs.protocols: any (custom routing; impedance control not offered by JLC flex)

price.note: JLCPCB home page 2026-09-30: 'Flexible PCBs ... From $2.00 / 5 pcs, Build Time: 5-6 days' (entry price for a small 1-2 layer FPC; real cost needs a quote).

parts.notes: JLC capability page: min bend radius 1-layer >=6x total thickness, multilayer >=10x; dynamic bending >=10-15x with 1-2 layers on adhesiveless PI; keep vias and pads out of the bend; 4-layer suits static bends only. A 0.11 mm 2-layer flex in dynamic use therefore needs about a 1.1-1.7 mm bend radius. Routing it around an outer two-pin link means the flex must loop outside or through the pin axis. JLC does not offer impedance control on flex, so a high-speed USB/MIPI flex needs a fab that does. IPC-2223 itself was not opened; the ratios are JLC's.

tactics.name: Continuous die-cut PSA ring between cover glass/display module and frame
tactics.method: Die-cut one closed-loop ring (no butt joints, corners radiused) from foam PSA; apply to frame ledge, press display with fixture at controlled pressure, dwell before leak test. Foam absorbs flatness tolerance; PET-core tapes need flatter parts.
tactics.design_rule: Tape thickness 0.10-0.30 mm (tesa 61365 0.10, 61395 0.20, 62626 0.30; VHB 5906 0.15 +/-15 %). Full VHB strength needs 72 h dwell at 21-38 C, surfaces cleaned with 50:50 IPA/water (3M). Unsourced starting points to verify by pressure-decay: ring width >=1.0-1.5 mm everywhere, no gap or overlap at the loop closure, ledge flatness better than half the foam thickness.
tactics.cost_note: Prototype: tesa 61395 1 mm x 33 m $8.95 (iFixit) or VHB 5906 1/2 in x 72 yd $68.66 plus die-cut. Production: converter die-cut, quote-only.

tactics.name: Back glass / rear cover PSA ring
tactics.method: Same closed-loop die-cut ring as the display; if the back must be serviceable, use PET-core tape (cleaner release) and design a pull-tab or heat-release path.
tactics.design_rule: Same thickness band 0.10-0.30 mm; keep camera/coil cut-outs inside the ring so the ring stays one unbroken loop. Ring width rule is an unsourced starting point (>=1.0-1.5 mm); validate by leak test.
tactics.cost_note: Same tapes as display bond; no extra part cost beyond die-cut.

tactics.name: Frame / midframe seams and screw bosses
tactics.method: Prefer a unibody frame so the only seams are the two glued lids. Where a joint is unavoidable (antenna splits, insert-molded plastic breaks), mold them as fused/insert-molded joints, not mechanical; any screw through the wet side gets its own O-ring or foam washer.
tactics.design_rule: Parker static O-ring rules: squeeze 19-32 % (face-seal table, 1.78 mm CS), max 30 % static, min squeeze about 0.2 mm; gland fill 60-85 % (75 % optimum), leave >=10 % void; ID stretch <=5 %; sealing surface <=32 uin (0.8 um) Ra-class, <=16 uin for gas face seals. Foam: PORON 4701-15 0.53-1.00 mm, 2.0-4.6 kPa at 25 % deflection (dust seal).
tactics.cost_note: O-rings cents each (price not verified); PORON via converter quote.

tactics.name: Sealed USB-C receptacle with O-ring to housing bore
tactics.method: Use a receptacle with an internal potted/sealed contact block (IP68-rated) and an O-ring around the shell that seals radially into a bored pocket in the frame; the connector opening stays wet, the phone interior stays dry.
tactics.design_rule: Design the frame pocket per the Same Sky datasheet O-ring drawing; apply Parker radial-seal rules (squeeze <=30 %, gland fill 60-85 %). Mid-mount heights: UJ20 2.7 mm, UJ32 2.0 mm. Datasheets state 'IP68' without depth/time, so verify at your IPX8 depth.
tactics.cost_note: UJ20 $2.78, UJ32 $4.29 qty1 at DigiKey; the O-ring bore adds frame machining but no extra part.

tactics.name: Speaker and receiver ports: ePTFE acoustic vent + outer dust mesh
tactics.method: Stack from outside in: grille slot -> woven dust mesh (optional) -> PSA-mounted ePTFE vent ring bonded to the housing boss -> gasketed speaker boot. The vent carries the water; mesh only keeps lint/metal dust off the membrane.
tactics.design_rule: Vent ring bonded on a boss with surface roughness VDI 15-21 (Gore install guide), clean with IPA, gloves, don't touch the active area. Largest standard IP68 Gore sizes: 3.0/6.0, 4.0/8.0, 5.0/9.4 mm, 0.31 mm thick. Gore rates speaker use case-by-case (table is for mics).

tactics.name: Microphone ports: IP68 ePTFE acoustic vents
tactics.method: One vent per MEMS mic port, bonded over the housing hole on the inside; keep the back cavity small (Gore data assumes 1 mm long, 1 mm diameter port).
tactics.design_rule: Typical loss at 1 kHz for ID 1.6 mm: GAW342 0.7 dB (IP68 5 m/30 min), GAW334 1.4 dB (IP68 2 m/60 min), GAW337 0.5 dB, GAW348 0.4 dB (IP67). Smaller ID raises loss (GAW337 at ID 1.0 mm about 2.6 dB). Total thickness 0.23-0.40 mm.

tactics.name: Barometer / internal pressure-equalization vent
tactics.method: A sealed phone must still breathe: a dedicated ePTFE pressure vent (not acoustic) keeps the barometer accurate, stops acoustic membranes bulging with temperature/altitude and stops the glue rings being pumped. Place it over a hidden hole (e.g. inside SIM slot or speaker grille).
tactics.design_rule: Pick by rating vs airflow: PE13 19,000 ml/min/cm2 @70 mbar (IP68 1.5 m/30 min); PE7 290 (IP68 2 m/1 h); PE15 380 (ISO 50 m/10 min); PE17 290 (ISO 100 m/15 min). Sizes ID/OD 1.6/3.8 to 5.5/10.2 mm.

tactics.name: Side buttons: O-ring on plunger shaft
tactics.method: Plunger slides through a bore in the frame; a micro O-ring in a groove on the plunger (or in the bore) seals radially; the dome switch sits on the dry side.
tactics.design_rule: Parker: dynamic squeeze max about 16 % (small cross-sections up to 25 %); static up to 30 %; min squeeze about 0.2 mm; gland fill 60-85 %; ID stretch <=5 %. For 2-001 (CS 1.02 mm) 20-25 % squeeze means groove depth about 0.77-0.82 mm (derived). Bore/plunger surface finish <=32 uin.
tactics.cost_note: Standard AS568 size, no tooling; price not verified.

tactics.name: Side buttons: overmolded LSR membrane / boot
tactics.method: An LSR boot or membrane is molded (or press-fitted with ribs) into the frame opening; the key cap pushes through the membrane, so there is no sliding seal at all. Better long-term than an O-ring on a moving shaft.
tactics.design_rule: Durometer 20-80 Shore A available; molded tolerance to +/-0.076 mm (Apple Rubber). Press-in-place ribbed designs prevent seal displacement. Membrane thickness/stroke rules not found in sources.

tactics.name: SIM tray gasket
tactics.method: LSR or silicone gasket molded onto (or stretched into a groove on) the tray's inner flange; it seals radially against the frame slot when the tray is seated. Or drop the physical SIM and use eSIM only to delete this leak path.
tactics.design_rule: Treat as a static radial seal: Parker squeeze <=30 %, min about 0.2 mm, gland fill 60-85 %. Unsourced: add a hard stop so the tray always seats at the same depth.

tactics.name: Internal nano/conformal coating as a second barrier
tactics.method: Coat the PCBA (and optionally the inside of the housing) after mechanical sealing is designed, as defense-in-depth against a failed seal or condensation. Mask connectors, contacts, sensors.
tactics.design_rule: HZO: Parylene 'IPX8+, also depends on device design'; do not claim an IP rating from coating alone. Coating thickness per HZO quote.
tactics.cost_note: HZO from $0.10/unit plus fixture NRE; P2i per-unit with in-factory equipment.

tactics.name: LSR overmolding of seals onto plastic/metal parts
tactics.method: Two-shot or insert molding of LSR directly onto the frame insert, button cap, SIM tray or speaker boot so the seal cannot be lost or misplaced during assembly; bond by primer or self-adhesive LSR grade.
tactics.design_rule: LSR suits complex profiles (low viscosity, LIM). Self-adhesive LSR grade/primer data not found in fetched sources.

tests.name: IP5X dust protected
tests.requirement: Ingress of dust is not entirely prevented, but it must not enter in sufficient quantity to interfere with satisfactory/safe operation.
tests.notes: IEC page returned 403; text from Wikipedia summary of IEC 60529.

tests.name: IP6X dust-tight
tests.requirement: No ingress of dust. A vacuum must be applied; test duration of up to 8 hours based on airflow.
tests.notes: Vented designs rely on the ePTFE membranes (Gore tests IP6X particle protection over 1-10 um particles).

tests.name: IPX7 temporary immersion
tests.requirement: Immersion 30 min with the lowest point of the enclosure 1,000 mm below the surface, or the highest point 150 mm below the surface, whichever is deeper; no harmful ingress.

tests.name: IPX8 continuous immersion
tests.requirement: Conditions (depth and time) specified by the manufacturer, more severe than IPX7; typically up to 3 m. The claim must state depth/time (e.g. 1.5 m 30 min, 2 m 30 min, 6 m 30 min).
tests.notes: Gore component ratings: vents to 2 m/60 min, 5 m/30 min; Gore says its vents let smartphones be protected at 4-6 m for 30 min.

tests.name: Water resistance to overpressure (component vents)
tests.requirement: Used by Gore to rate GAW344 (50 m/10 min), GAW346 (100 m/15 min), PE15 (50 m/10 min), PE17 (100 m/15 min); Gore also runs its own eWEP (extended water entry pressure) test at membrane and product level.
tests.notes: Component rating, not a device rating.

tests.name: Pressure decay / differential pressure decay
tests.requirement: Cincinnati Test Systems: pressure decay for open parts sealed and pressurized internally, leak rates 1-10 sccm; differential pressure decay for lower leak rates 0.5-5 sccm; tracer gas sniff/accumulation <7 sccm.
tests.notes: No published air-leak to water-ingress correlation; set the reject limit by testing known-good and deliberately-leaking (pin-holed) golden samples against dunk tests (engineering practice, unsourced).
equipment: Cincinnati Test Systems pressure decay / mass flow

tests.name: Sealed-device chamber (volumetric fill / bell) test
tests.requirement: For a finished phone with no test port: place it in a sealed chamber, pressurize (or evacuate) the chamber and measure decay in the space around the part; a gross-leak stage first, then fine decay.
tests.notes: ePTFE vents pass air by design, so either blank them with a fixture seal or set the limit to include their known airflow. ATEQ lists F620 volume/bell-test capability for electronics waterproof testing; no leak-rate numbers published.

tests.name: Dunk test at claimed IPX8 depth + indicator paper
tests.requirement: Before certification: pressure-pot or tank test at the claimed depth/time with water-contact indicator labels inside; then open and inspect. Repeat after drop and thermal cycling to catch adhesive creep.
tests.notes: Procedure is common practice, not from a cited standard; test-lab prices for IEC 60529 certification were not found (search budget exhausted).

Battery items drop out if the pack vendor supplies UN38.3 + IEC 62133-2 reports.

guidance.title: Keep NdFeB latch magnets away from the e-compass; hard-iron offsets drift with temperature
guidance.finding: Bosch BMM350 handling/placement guide (BST-BMM350-HS000-08, rev 1.8) says hard magnets (NdFeB, ferrite) near the sensor create offsets that sensor-fusion calibration must subtract, and that these offsets drift with temperature: in a 500 uT ferrite offset field the offset moves 10 uT per 10 °C (0.2 %/K), enough to break heading. Soft-magnetic parts (steel shields, hinge pins, mu-metal) bend the field and are very hard to correct in software, so keep them away from the sensor. A 100 mA trace 5 mm away is also a measurable disturbance. Put the magnetometer at the far end of the half without the latch magnets, and use non-magnetic stainless (austenitic 304/316) or titanium hinge pins.

guidance.title: Magnetometer full-scale and recovery after strong magnets
guidance.finding: BMM350 (datasheet BST-BMM350-DS001-27, rev 1.27): full-scale +/-2000 uT, tested against field shocks up to 400 mT (250-400 mT does not damage it), and z-axis hysteresis after a full-scale sweep is cleared by a 'magnetic reset' that the device runs every ODR tick in normal/forced mode. MEMSIC MMC5603NJ: field range 30 G (3 mT), disturbing field 32 G, maximum exposed field 10,000 G; fields above about 30 G can flip the AMR film, which the on-chip SET/RESET strap then restores. The static field of the closed-lid magnets at the sensor must therefore stay well under the sensor range (a few mT at most for AMR parts), or the compass saturates whenever the phone is shut.

guidance.title: AMR compass parts are upset by fields above ~3 mT
guidance.finding: MEMSIC MMC5603NJ datasheet: 30 G total field range, 32 G disturbing field, 10,000 G maximum exposure. A strong field over 30 G in any direction can flip the sensing film's polarity, and a SET/RESET pulse is needed to restore accuracy. Check the latch-magnet field at the compass with K&J's field calculator before fixing the layout.

guidance.title: Accessory rule: do not trigger repeated compass recalibration
guidance.finding: Apple Accessory Design Guidelines R31 (2026-09-21): accessories for devices with a digital compass 'shall minimize interference with the digital compass and shall not repeatedly trigger compass recalibration', and cases are verified with a magnetometer test (sec. 5.10.8). K&J Magnetics tested NdFeB car mounts on phones and found mapping apps kept working with only minor initial heading errors. Treat the latch magnets as a fixed hard-iron offset that the OS calibration learns, and keep that offset the same open and shut (or switch calibration sets using the lid Hall sensor).

guidance.title: Magnets near wireless charging: the MagSafe/Qi2 numbers
guidance.finding: Apple ADG R31 ch. 42: MagSafe accessory magnets shall be N48H NdFeB with 7-13 um NiCuNi plating, Br 13.7-14.1 kGs, Hcj >= 17 kOe, BHmax 45-48 MGOe, flux density at the product surface <= 0.215 T. They must self-align within 1.55 mm radially, the case dislodge force target is 1000-1300 gf, and keep-out is 30 mm from the ring centre plus 6 mm clearance beyond it. Integrated arrays 'shall not interfere with inductive charging'. Qi transmitters must be Qi v2.0+ certified (v2.2+ recommended), and Apple recommends shielding the charging coil's magnetic field. For a flip phone, keep the latch magnets outside the Qi coil's ferrite and the 30 mm attach zone, and use H/SH grade magnets since coils heat the back.

guidance.title: Magnet pull force falls steeply with gap; datasheet numbers are best case
guidance.finding: K&J Magnetics: 'Pull Force Case 1' is one magnet on a thick, flat, ground steel plate. Case 2 (between two plates) can be much higher for thin magnets, e.g. a D82 goes from 6.44 lb to 16 lb. A small gap cuts force sharply: the D82's 6.44 lb drops to about 3 lb with a 0.03 in (0.76 mm) paper gap. Two magnets sliding in shear keep only about 50 % of the listed force. For a magnet-to-magnet latch through two 0.5 mm shell walls, budget well under half the catalog Case 1 figure and check it with K&J's gap calculator.

guidance.title: Dynamic flex across a hinge: bend radius >= 10-15x thickness
guidance.finding: JLCPCB flex capability page: minimum bend radius is >= 6x total thickness for single-layer and >= 10x for multilayer; dynamic (repeated) bending needs >= 10-15x, with 1-2 layers on adhesiveless polyimide, no vias or pads in the bend, and 4-layer flex for static bends only. These are the commonly quoted IPC-2223 style ratios; the IPC standard itself (paywalled) was not opened. A 0.11 mm 2-layer flex needs a radius of about 1.1-1.7 mm, so an outer-link hinge needs a service loop or a contactless link (ST60A3H1) instead.

guidance.title: Current foldables: IP48 and teardrop/multi-rail hinges
guidance.finding: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip7 and Z Fold7 (2025) are rated IP48, which Samsung defines as 'resists solid particles >1 mm; tested for submersion in up to 5 feet of fresh water for up to 30 minutes'. Both use the 'Armor FlexHinge', a water-droplet (teardrop) fold with a new multi-rail structure that spreads stress and reduces the crease, in Advanced Armor Aluminum hinge housing (Fold7 newsroom). The '4' means dust ingress is not sealed below 1 mm; real foldables do not claim IP6x because the hinge cannot be dust-sealed. Samsung's pages fetched did not state a fold-cycle count.

guidance.title: Motorola razr 2026 family: titanium-reinforced hinge
guidance.finding: Motorola's 2026 razr launch (razr ultra 2026 at $1,499.99, razr+ and razr) cites a 'titanium-reinforced hinge refined over multiple razr generations' for longevity. The release fetched did not state an IP rating or a fold-cycle count, so do not assume one. For an outer-link hinge, titanium or hardened stainless links and pins follow the same practice.

guidance.title: MagSafe numbers to copy for the Duo dock: 1.55 mm self-align, 650-1510 gf attach
guidance.finding: Apple ADG R31 (2026-09-21) sec. 42: case and accessory magnet arrays must magnetically self-align within 1.55 mm radial. Accessory-to-device dislodge force (normal to the back) must be 650-1510 gf (Table 42-3); cases target 1000-1300 gf and are verified at 800-1100 gf with a force gauge averaged over 5 pulls. Accessory magnets N48H (Br 13.7-14.1 kGs, Hcj >= 17 kOe, NiCuNi 7-13 um), case magnets N45SH (Hcj >= 20.5 kOe, epoxy), surface flux <= 0.215 T, DC shield low-carbon steel 1010/DT4 with Bsat >= 2.0 T, keep-in 30 mm radius plus 6 mm clearance. No shear/slide force is specified. Apple's recommended array vendors are Baotou INST Magnetic, Ningbo Sanhuan Magsound and Quadrant Solutions. For two 69 mm pieces stacked back-to-back, a full MagSafe ring fits; for side-by-side docking use edge bars and budget a 1.55 mm alignment error at the pogo pads.

guidance.title: Qi2 MPP: magnets are mandatory but the numbers are member-only
guidance.finding: WPC: Qi2 launched November 2023 at 15 W with magnetic attachment (Magnetic Power Profile); Qi v2.2.1 'Qi2 25W' launched July 23, 2025 with 14 devices certified in a limited launch, and over 1.5 billion certified Qi2 devices within a year. WPC's public pages give no magnet dimensions, grade or force; those are in the Qi v2.x specification for members. Use Apple ADG numbers as the public proxy and buy rings already sold for Qi2/MagSafe (e.g. totalelement-r54x46x15mmn52-5pk).

guidance.title: Pogo pins are not sealed by themselves: seal the housing, run at mid-stroke
guidance.finding: Mill-Max FAQ: its spring-loaded pins 'are not IP rated'; when the plunger compresses it moves into the body and 'will create an entry point for liquids or contaminants', so waterproof designs put the pins in a housing sealed with gaskets or O-rings. Run pins at mid-stroke; most Mill-Max pins are cycle-tested to 100,000-1,000,000 cycles at mid-stroke; the highest discrete pin is 13 A, derated 20 % to 10.4 A. Pins can mate any conductive surface, but dedicated gold target contacts are recommended. For the Duo, put sprung pins on one piece behind an O-ring/overmould and flat gold targets flush on the other, so the exposed side has no moving seal.

guidance.title: Exposed pads: film resistance, gold, working height and pad size vs alignment
guidance.finding: CFE: pogo failures come from contaminated surfaces, worn plating, fatigued springs, misalignment and over-current; a film of skin oil or sweat dominates contact resistance because a pogo tip has small area and modest force, so use gold, recess or shield the pins, and clean with IPA. Working height (where force is specified, e.g. BP13501: 5.50 mm, 100 g +/-20 %) is not the free length or full stroke; over-compression shortens life. Design inference (not from a standard): make each target pad radius at least the magnetic self-align error (about 1.55 mm for MagSafe-class arrays) plus the plunger tip radius, and keep pad-to-pad pitch above twice that so a misaligned pin never bridges two pads.

guidance.title: Android spanning across two screens: Jetpack WindowManager + OEM extensions
guidance.finding: Android docs: FoldingFeature reports bounds, state (FLAT/HALF_OPENED), orientation, occlusionType (NONE/FULL) and isSeparating, which 'is always true on a dual-screen device when the application spans both screens'. The OEM must ship the WindowManager Extensions library (inherit window_extensions.mk, deployed to system_ext), declare the seam in config_display_features (e.g. 'fold-[1000,0,1000,2000]'), map postures in config_device_state_postures and configure device_state_configuration.xml; CDD 7.1.1.1 requires it for devices with a hinge joining separate panels; vendor API level 6 on Android 15. androidx.window stable 1.5.1 (Nov 19, 2025), 1.6.0-alpha05 (Jun 17, 2026). For the hinge-less Duo, the dock Hall sensors must drive DeviceStateManager so the two docked panels report one separating 'hinge' with occlusionType FULL.

guidance.title: Surface Duo dual-screen SDK is archived; the web API is still experimental
guidance.finding: Microsoft's Surface Duo SDK docs now live under learn.microsoft.com/previous-versions (marked archived, last updated 2024-12-17); they point Android apps to Jetpack WindowManager rather than a Microsoft SDK. On the web, MDN lists the Viewport Segments API (window.viewport.segments, viewport-segment env() variables, horizontal-/vertical-viewport-segments media features) as experimental with limited availability. Do not plan on Microsoft-specific dual-screen APIs; use Jetpack WindowManager and treat web spanning as progressive enhancement.

guidance.title: T-Mobile DIGITS: one number on several devices through an app
guidance.finding: T-Mobile support (2026-09-30): DIGITS gives 'one phone number on multiple devices or multiple numbers on one device', managed in the DIGITS app (Android/iOS) or web client; access is free on all T-Mobile postpaid lines; up to 5 numbers on one device; a DIGITS Talk & Text line can be shared with up to 20 people. Calls ride the app over data, not the second device's own SIM, so the Duo's second piece could ring for the same number through the DIGITS app without its own modem.

guidance.title: Verizon Number Share: host phone plus watches/Palm only, $15/month each
guidance.finding: Verizon FAQ (2026-09-30): a host smartphone shares its number with up to 5 connected devices, LTE network only; eligible connected devices are listed smartwatches and the Palm companion phone (Palm 'can only act as your primary phone' in the current list); $15/month plus taxes per wearable or Palm; postpaid only. A second smartphone-class piece is not an eligible connected device, so a Duo with two modems cannot share one Verizon number this way; give only one piece a modem and relay calls over the dock/BLE.

guidance.title: AT&T NumberSync: number on tablets, watches, computers, cars
guidance.finding: AT&T (2026-09-30): NumberSync syncs 'your smartphone number' with 'your tablet, smartwatch, computer, select vehicles, and compatible devices'; the cellular Apple Watch version needs its own watch plan and works on the AT&T domestic network (plus Mexico and Canada). Like Verizon, it is built for companion device types, not a second phone, so certification of a custom second piece as a NumberSync device is unlikely; plan one modem per Duo.

fabs.name: JLCPCB HDI (laser blind vias, 1/2/3-step)

fabs.notes: HDI FAQ dated 2026-09-07; service announced 2026-09-14. Laser via 0.075-0.15 mm, default 0.1 mm (so default pad 0.25 mm by the +0.15 rule; 0.225 mm is the rule applied to the 0.075 mm minimum). Trace/space 3/3 mil standard, 3.5/3.5 mil recommended, 2.7/2.7 mil 'extreme'. Different-net hole-edge spacing >= 0.24 mm; mechanical aspect ratio <= 16:1; blind via depth:diameter <= 1:1; HDI max thickness 2.4 mm. 1st/2nd/3rd order = 1/2/3 lamination + laser cycles (structure names 1+N+1 etc. are the standard mapping, not JLC wording). FAQ defines the stacked via type (blind and buried vias aligned at the same position); staggered is not explicitly stated. Impedance +-10% for >=50 ohm, +-5 ohm below 50 ohm. Laminates Shengyi and Nanya; the PP table is an image only. layers_max 32 and min thickness 0.4 mm are from the general rigid capability page, not HDI-specific. min_bga_pitch_mm is the Standard PCBA assembly limit, not stated for HDI fab.

materials.name: JLCPCB HDI stackup naming (e.g. JLCH081611Y2-1078A)
materials.notes: JLC HDI stackup per-layer thicknesses are not published as a table; only the naming rule (image): JLC + H (HDI) + layer count (2 digits) + board thickness (08=0.8 mm, 11=1.1 mm, 16=1.6 mm) + outer Cu (1=1 oz) + inner Cu (1=1 oz, H=0.5 oz) + buried via N/Y + HDI order (1/2/3, A=any-layer) + '-' + outer-layer PP (e.g. 1078, 1037, 2313) + suffix letter. Examples shown: JLCH101611N1-1078A, JLCH06161HY2-1037B, JLCH08081HY3-2313C. Layer details only visible in the order form.

duo_notes.title: Jetpack WindowManager FoldingFeature / isSeparating
duo_notes.finding: Jetpack WindowManager (WindowInfoTracker -> WindowLayoutInfo) reports a FoldingFeature with state (FLAT / HALF_OPENED), orientation (HORIZONTAL / VERTICAL), occlusionType (NONE / FULL), bounds and isSeparating. isSeparating is always true on dual-screen devices when an app spans both screens, so a hinge/gap between two panels is modelled as a FULL-occlusion FoldingFeature. Latest androidx.window: 1.5.1 stable (2025-11-19), 1.6.0-alpha05 (2026-06-17).

duo_notes.title: WindowManager Extensions are OEM system code
duo_notes.finding: The FoldingFeature data comes from WindowManager Extensions, an opt-in platform module the OEM compiles into a JAR on the system_ext partition. Window layout info is required for foldable devices with hinges; Window Area (rear display / dual-display mode) applies to devices with an Android-compatible cover display. Implication for Amni Duo: spanning one app across both pieces only works out of the box if one Android instance owns both panels (both DSI panels on the primary SoC, e.g. companion panel driven over a docking connector); two separate processors need custom display streaming, and the Extensions must report the gap as a hinge.
duo_notes.verify_notes: AOSP page opened 2026-09-30. The Amni Duo implication is our inference, not text from the page.

duo_notes.title: Surface Duo SDK is archived; its guidance points to Jetpack WindowManager
duo_notes.finding: Microsoft moved the Surface Duo SDK docs to the previous-versions archive (is_archived: true, updated 2024-12-17). The archived Window Manager page says Jetpack WindowManager provides a standard API for all foldables, that the Duo dual-screen library works on top of it, and that isSeparating is always true when an app spans the Duo hinge. Use androidx.window, not the Duo SDK, for new work.
duo_notes.verify_notes: Both Microsoft Learn pages opened 2026-09-30 (archive metadata shows is_archived true).

duo_notes.title: Android multi-display and multi-resume
duo_notes.finding: AOSP multi-display: a device always has DEFAULT_DISPLAY; secondary displays can be private, mirrored, trusted for user tasks, or used with the Presentation API, with multi-resume, per-display IME support and independent input routing. Multi-resume is standard from Android 10 (API 29); Android 11 (API 30) added window metrics for other displays (Jetpack WindowManager backports to API 14).
duo_notes.verify_notes: AOSP and Android Developers pages opened 2026-09-30.

duo_notes.title: CompanionDeviceManager pairing profiles
duo_notes.finding: CompanionDeviceManager (Android 8.0 / API 26+) scans BLE/Wi-Fi for the app and pairs without ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION; paired apps may run, use data and start foreground services in the background. Android 12+ adds profiles: Watch, Glasses, App Streaming, Computer, Nearby Device Streaming. A Duo companion app on the primary would pair the companion piece through this API.

duo_notes.title: Wi-Fi Direct measured throughput on stock Android
duo_notes.finding: Wi-Fi Direct lets devices form their own Wi-Fi network without an access point (Wi-Fi Alliance; WPA2 + WPS per Wikipedia; in Android since 4.0, 2011). Measured stock-Android peak receiver throughput (arXiv 2604.07889, 2026, five Samsung Galaxy A10s): ~19.7 Mbit/s with 2 devices in 1 group, ~16 Mbit/s across 3 groups. Budget 2.4/5 GHz Wi-Fi 4/5 handsets, so treat it as a floor; no newer Wi-Fi 6/7 P2P measurement was found.
duo_notes.verify_notes: Wi-Fi Alliance, Wikipedia and arXiv abstract opened 2026-09-30. Neither Wi-Fi Alliance nor Wikipedia gives a number; the only figure is the arXiv measurement.

duo_notes.title: Wi-Fi Aware (NAN) on Android
duo_notes.finding: Wi-Fi Aware (Android 8.0 / API 26+) discovers and connects devices directly with no AP and "support[s] higher throughput rates across longer distances than Bluetooth connections". From Android 12 the responder can accept any peer, which speeds up data-path setup and allows several point-to-point links from one request. The page gives no Mbps figure.

duo_notes.title: Bluetooth LE data throughput (1M vs 2M PHY)
duo_notes.finding: BLE 1M PHY signals at 1 Mbps and 2M PHY roughly doubles throughput at reduced range; max application payload is 244 B per packet with Data Length Extension (Nordic DevAcademy). Calculated max application throughput (Novel Bits): ~1,400 kbps on 2M PHY (247 B ATT MTU, DLE, no encryption, one direction) and ~661 kbps on 1M PHY. That is enough for touch/sensor/control traffic and compressed audio, not for raw display frames.
duo_notes.verify_notes: Nordic DevAcademy and Novel Bits pages opened 2026-09-30. The Novel Bits numbers are theoretical best cases, as the article itself says.

duo_notes.title: Bluetooth LE Audio / LC3
duo_notes.finding: Bluetooth SIG: in listening tests LC3 beats SBC on quality "even at a 50% lower bit rate"; LE Audio adds Multi-Stream (independent, synchronised streams to one or more sinks) and Auracast broadcast to an unlimited number of sinks, and the LE Audio specifications are complete. LC3 arrived around Bluetooth 5.2 (Wikipedia). Fraunhofer LC3plus supports 10 / 7.5 / 5 / 2.5 / 1.25 ms frames and up to 96 kHz (ETSI, not royalty-free and not interoperable with LC3).
duo_notes.verify_notes: Bluetooth SIG, Wikipedia and Fraunhofer IIS pages opened 2026-09-30. None of them gives an LC3 bitrate range or latency figure, so none is recorded.

duo_notes.title: UWB relative positioning (FiRa / Android UWB)
duo_notes.finding: FiRa: UWB uses 500 MHz channels with ~2 ns pulses for centimetre ranging by time of flight (two-way challenge/response). FiRa supports channels 5-14, and channel 9 is the only one mandatory for FiRa Certified devices. Android Jetpack UWB (Android 12+, android.hardware.uwb) states 10 cm ranging precision, is FiRa MAC 1.3 compliant with static or provisioned STS (provisioned on Android 14+), and needs an out-of-band channel (e.g. BLE) to exchange session parameters between controller and controlee. Enough to tell the two Duo pieces apart and how far apart they are before docking.
duo_notes.verify_notes: FiRa and Android Developers pages opened 2026-09-30. Neither page gives an angle-of-arrival accuracy figure.

duo_notes.title: UWB chip-level range / AoA accuracy
duo_notes.finding: Per entries already in compute-radio.json: Qorvo QM35825 lists 5 cm ranging and 2 deg AoA (4 antennas, FiRa 3.0); Qorvo QM33120W lists 10 cm and 5 deg (2 antennas); Qorvo DWM3000 module lists <15 cm (2D) / <30 cm (3D).
duo_notes.verify_notes: qorvo.com returned HTTP 429 and web.archive.org is blocked for this fetcher on 2026-09-30, so the figures were not re-opened here; they come from compute-radio.json (qorvo-qm35825, qorvo-qm33120w, qorvo-dwm3000).

duo_notes.title: eSIM Multiple Enabled Profiles (Android 13+)
duo_notes.finding: MEP (Android 13+) lets a single eUICC hold profiles on several ports with one enabled profile per port, giving dual SIM dual standby on one eSIM chip. The OEM must integrate it with the SoC and eSIM vendors, implement the MEP IRadio AIDL HAL, declare android.hardware.telephony.euicc.mep, and ship an LPA that supports multiple ports. eSIM specs: SGP.22 (consumer), SGP.02 (M2M), SGP.32 (IoT, published May 2023); devices can store 20+ profiles with 1-2 active (Wikipedia).
duo_notes.verify_notes: AOSP MEP page and Wikipedia eSIM opened 2026-09-30.

duo_notes.title: GSMA TS.43 ODSA: companion-device subscription activation
duo_notes.finding: GSMA TS.43 Service Entitlement Configuration (resource page dated 2024-07-17) covers On-Device Service Activation of eSIM devices (Primary, Companion and/or Enterprise): an ODSA client app on one device entitles and activates a companion device subscription with the operator. Carriers use this mechanism for shared-number watches. The page does not name smartwatches or MSISDN sharing explicitly.
duo_notes.verify_notes: GSMA resource page opened 2026-09-30 (the ODSA overview page returned 403). The link to carrier watch plans is general industry knowledge, not stated on the page.

duo_notes.title: Single-number multi-device carrier plans are watch/tablet only
duo_notes.finding: Vodafone UK OneNumber shares a phone plan with cellular smartwatches (Apple Watch S3+, Galaxy Watch 4G+, Pixel Watch, OPPO Watch, others) and eSIM tablets "from just GBP 7.50 a month"; the page lists no phones as OneNumber devices and gives no device cap. Verizon Number Share, AT&T NumberSync and T-Mobile DIGITS pages could not be opened (404/403). Implication: a cellular companion piece would likely need to be provisioned as a watch-class device via TS.43 ODSA (OEM + carrier certification), or the companion carries no cellular and relays through the primary.
duo_notes.verify_notes: Vodafone page opened 2026-09-30. Verizon (302 to 404), AT&T (404) and T-Mobile (403) could not be read. The implication is our inference.

BLM + size (03=0201, 15=0402, 18=0603) + type (AX/AG/PX/KG) + impedance at 100 MHz, 3-digit ohm code (121=120 ohm, 221=220 ohm, 241=240 ohm, 601=600 ohm) + SN1D. Use listed MPNs.
